sections.overview: A marine snailfish in the family Liparidae, it is known from the northeast Atlantic south of Iceland.
sections.identification: The species description notes pale skin, an unpigmented head beneath the skin, and a steeply angled mouth.
sections.habitat: FishBase reports a bathydemersal, deep-water occurrence; the source gives a depth range, but this entry avoids treating sparse records as a full ecological limit.
sections.diet: The consulted species accounts do not describe its diet.
sections.behavior: Species-specific behavior is not reported in the consulted accounts.
sections.reproduction: No species-specific reproductive information is given in the consulted sources.
sections.ecology: The published record is sparse, and the consulted sources provide little ecological information beyond its locality and deep-water association. P. cathetostomus is a congener from the eastern Pacific, described with a similarly steeply angled mouth. P. spirohira is another northeast-Atlantic congener, recorded west of northern Spain; its description emphasizes a coiled intestine.
sections.conservation: FishBase lists the species as not evaluated by the IUCN.
